messages:
sara: Quick sync — proposing a small, launchable surface for the function-call API we can ship in Q2. Need alignment on scope & must-have launch criteria. TL;DR: define a compact call envelope + result envelope, opt-in schema validation, streaming partial results, and clear fallback/error semantics.

kevin: +1. Can you paste the minimal shapes you have in mind? want to check runtime impact (validation cost, extra RPC fields).

sara: Sure. Minimal idea: request: { model, input, tools:[{name,schema_version}], call_policy:{timeout,allow_partial} } response: { type: "tool_call" | "tool_result" | "fallback_text", payload: string | json, schema_version, status:{ok|error|partial}, error_code? }.

maria: For runtime we need to avoid heavy JSON Schema validation per-call. Suggest an opt-in contract: api accepts a declared schema_version; runtime only enforces lightweight shape checks (presence/types) and surfaces a validation score in telemetry. Full strict validation can be a beta opt-in.

kevin: agree on opt-in. Otherwise every request pays parse/validate tax. We can add a signed schema manifest fetched infrequently and cached per-deployment.

 daniel: UX question — do we return raw JSON for tool results or wrap with metadata (exec_time, node_id)? customers often ask for traceability.

 sara: Launch: include exec_time and tool_id (no node_id for now). Keep envelope small. Add optional verbose flag for debug mode.

 eva: Security: tool result envelope must allow an integrity signature header if the tool is external (third-party). Also we need to define what "fallback_text" means for PII/filtered outputs — must include a reason code.

 kevin: Implementation note: streaming partial tool results complicates schema validation. Propose two modes: streaming-bytes (opaque) and streaming-json-chunks (line-delimited JSON) with a finalization event that includes final status & schema_version.

 sara: Good call. For launch we can support streaming-bytes only; streaming-json-chunks comes in a later milestone. Launch criteria: 1) SDKs accept call/result envelopes, 2) fallback_text well-defined with reason codes, 3) opt-in schema validation with cached manifests, 4) telemetry + regression alerts for schema mismatches.

 maria: Also add "maximum serialized size" per tool response for quotas. Helps Dedicated customers plan capacity and avoids OOM on Private.

 daniel: Product ask: sample UX cases for ops teams. e.g., how to debug a failed call: logs should include schema_version, validation_score, tool_id, call_latency, and error_code. Can we commit to those fields being emitted?

 kevin: yes, we'll emit those fields to RedConsole traces. We'll also include a "validation_hint" string for quick troubleshooting.

 sara: Prioritization: must-have for Q2: call envelope + result envelope, fallback_text, opt-in schema validation (cached manifests), core telemetry. Nice-to-have Q2+: streaming JSON chunks, external signed tool results, verbose debug flag.

 eva: For compliance, Private installs will need an option to disable remote manifest fetch and to upload schema manifests via the console. Mark as required for Private launch.

 sara: Noted — add to Private launch checklist.

 deploy-bot: deployment scheduled: feature-flag rollout to alpha orgs starts 1958766000.

 kevin: Next steps: I'll draft a minimal open API-style spec and a lightweight SDK patch for call/result envelopes. Can we get product review on Wed?

 sara: Wed works. I'll prepare customer examples and prioritization rationale (3 anchor customers + one SRE scenario). Thanks all. :raised_hands:
